title: Chocolate ice cream
subtitle: Dark chocolate custard ice cream
excerpt: An intensely flavoured dark chocolate ice cream built on a crème anglaise base enriched with both cocoa and melted chocolate. Rich, creamy, and deeply chocolatey.
sourceNotes: Standard dark chocolate custard ice cream using a crème anglaise base. Method synthesised from multiple classic references including Jeni Britton Bauer and David Lebovitz, The Perfect Scoop (2007).

recipe.freezeNotes: Store in a sealed container for up to 6 weeks. Press baking parchment against the surface to prevent ice crystals.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The base must be completely cold before churning (minimum 4 hours, preferably overnight).

content.text: The double chocolate technique (cocoa in the custard base plus melted chocolate stirred in before churning) gives a deeper, more complex flavour than either ingredient alone. Use a 70% cocoa chocolate for the best flavour. The custard base is a standard crème anglaise.
Place the chopped dark chocolate in a large heatproof bowl. Set aside.
Whisk the cocoa powder into the cold milk until smooth. Pour into a saucepan with the cream. Warm over medium heat until just below boiling point.

Whisk the egg yolks, sugar, vanilla, and salt together in a bowl until pale. Pour the hot cocoa cream over the yolks in a slow stream, whisking constantly. Return to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring, until the custard coats the back of a spoon (about 82°C). Do not boil.
Pour the hot custard over the chopped chocolate. Stir gently until the chocolate is fully melted and smooth. Strain through a fine sieve. Refrigerate until completely cold (at least 4 hours).
Churn in an ice cream machine for 20 to 25 minutes until thick. Transfer to a container and freeze for 2 hours before serving. Remove 5 minutes before scooping.

items.fix: Cook over the lowest heat and stir constantly. At the first sign of curdling, pour immediately through a sieve into a cold bowl and blend.

items.symptom: The chocolate has lumps in the finished base
items.cause: Chocolate not finely chopped or custard not hot enough
items.fix: Chop the chocolate very finely. If lumps remain, blend the base and strain again.

items.symptom: The ice cream is too hard to scoop
items.fix: Leave at room temperature for 5 minutes. Adding a tablespoon of neutral spirit (vodka) before churning lowers the freezing point.

items.cause: Chocolate was too dark or cocoa over-measured
items.fix: Use 70% chocolate; 85% can be too intense for ice cream. Taste the base before churning and add a little more sugar.

content.text: Chocolate ice cream is the perennial rival to vanilla for the title of most ordered flavour. The custard base version is the most rewarding to make at home: it has a texture no commercial ice cream matches and a depth of chocolate flavour that depends entirely on the quality of the chocolate you use. Worth making with a 70% single-origin bar for a special occasion.
